new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is phonemic (contrastive), but the normal position is the penultimate syllable; a final syllable of shape CVV (a long vowel or vowel sequence, i.e. a heavy final) takes the stress instead. Syllable shapes are CV(V)(V) and CCV(V).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in this chapter (it is a nasalization study; stress is only in the six-line introductory section 0.4).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'normally' and the statement that stress is contrastive at word level, i.e. some words do not follow the penult/final-CVV default; no examples of exceptions are given in this chapter.
new_statements.identity_note: Both the chapter and the volume's foreword describe the language as 'Epena Pedee (Saija)', the Choco language of the Pacific coastal rivers of Colombia (Narino to southern Choco); the data come from speakers of the Guangui River tributary of the Saija River, collected 1977-1979 (chapter note 1). This is the Epena of epen1239, not Embera.

tone.quote: [p.24, sec. 7.1] Las vocales pueden llevar variaciones del sonido como el acento, el tono o la nasalidad. Algunas lenguas tienen un sistema de tonos sobre las vocales como el idioma chino. ... [p.29] En cuanto al acento, la mayoría de las palabras del sia pedee lo tienen en la penúltima sílaba, lo que en español se conoce como acento grave; entonces lo más práctico es no marcarlo. Cuando las palabras del sia pedee se pronuncian acentuadas en la última o penúltima sílaba en el alfabeto práctico, se marcarían con tilde como cuando se marca en español en las palabras agudas y esdrújulas.
tone.locator: p.24, sec. 7.1 'Sonidos vocalicos'; p.29, stress paragraph and table 'Escritura del acento' at the end of sec. 9 'Alfabeto practico para el sia pedee'
tone.translation: [p.24] Vowels can carry variations of sound such as accent (stress), tone or nasality. Some languages have a system of tones on the vowels, like Chinese. ... [p.29] As for stress, most sia pedee words have it on the penultimate syllable, what in Spanish is called 'acento grave'; so the most practical thing is not to mark it. When sia pedee words are pronounced stressed on the final or [ante]penultimate syllable, in the practical alphabet they would be marked with a written accent, as Spanish does for final-stressed and antepenult-stressed words.
